answer: the ladder moved the rule as intended -- across 30 cells the band changed the number of weight changes by -1139..-36 (total -12600), and the toll channel moved with it (81.1..398.5 bp/yr at x2 costs). The selection channel moved -246.5..303.1 bp/yr against it. 1 of 30 banded cells are called a fix (BAND_PAYS), 7 lose to the base arm (BAND_COSTS), 22 are point-estimate-only (BAND_NOISE), 0 save toll but not enough to cover the selection given up, 0 never move a weight, 0 unresolved. Bar: |t| >= 3.34 over 60 cells. 6 of 30 banded cells sit at or below 5 weight changes over the whole sample -- there the band has not slowed the rule, it has replaced it with a buy-and-hold at roughly the base exposure, so any toll saving in those cells is the null arm's zero-turnover, not a fix. None of the 1 cells called a fix is collapsed.

frozen_spec.band_scale: in-sample standard deviation of the volatility signal
frozen_spec.bar_basis: two-sided 5% over 60 cells x 2 cost levels
frozen_spec.const_weight: the base arm's own OOS average weight, frozen across rungs
frozen_spec.identity: pair = selection + sizing + toll, per session and per rung
frozen_spec.known_mechanical: the toll is linear in the cost parameter, so d_toll(x2) == 2*d_toll(x1); the x2 limb of the frozen condition cannot fail once x1 passes
frozen_spec.no_adoption: the base arms are already judged; this only asks whether one of their channels is purchasable
frozen_spec.rule: hold the committed weight until |v_i - v_at_last_commit| >= band
